data.content_ref: inline:exp-hist:{"target": "9b36b0954abeefe443e6ed3d049ec207c0b0f827afa35e5b1e9041fb5c427c33", "seq": 1, "objection": "The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) to justify preferring better-corroborated theories without induction, but this fails because Popper's own framework cannot coherently define or compare verisimilitude between false theories. Since all universal scientific theories are strictly false (falsified), and Popper rejected probabilistic measures, there is no non-inductive metric within his system to rank one false theory as 'closer to the truth' than another based solely on past test survival. The claim that surviving severe tests increases 'rational expectation' of verisimilitude implicitly assumes the future will resemble the past (that tests which worked before will continue to track truth), which is precisely the inductive principle Popper rejected. Thus, the preference either collapses into inductivism or lacks any rational basis within Popper's strictures.", "outcome": "raised and not answered; the target's status did not move"}
